en: Itivuttaka 50: Tikanipāta, Paṭhamavagga (The First Chapter) Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: “Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a young jasmine flower; the person who is like a blue lotus flower; and the person who is like a red lotus flower. And how, monks, is one a person like a young jasmine flower? Here, monks, a certain person is virtuous, possessed of good conduct, restrained with the restraint of the Pātimokkha, perfect in behavior and resort, and seeing fear in even the slightest faults, he trains himself by undertaking the training rules. He gains internal mental serenity, but does not gain the higher wisdom that is noble and transcendent, the penetration of the Dhamma. This, monks, is called a person like a young jasmine flower. And how, monks, is one a person like a blue lotus flower? Here, monks, a certain person is virtuous... [as above] ...he trains himself by undertaking the training rules. He gains internal mental serenity and also gains the higher wisdom that is noble and transcendent, the penetration of the Dhamma. Yet, while he dwells having attained this, he does not realize the fruit thereof, the state of non-returning. This, monks, is called a person like a blue lotus flower. And how, monks, is one a person like a red lotus flower? Here, monks, a certain person is virtuous... [as above] ...he trains himself by undertaking the training rules. He gains internal mental serenity and also gains the higher wisdom that is noble and transcendent, the penetration of the Dhamma. While dwelling having attained this, he realizes the fruit thereof, the state of non-returning. This, monks, is called a person like a red lotus flower. These, monks, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, a certain monk addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Friend Ānanda, what is the meaning of ‘a person like a young jasmine flower,’ ‘a person like a blue lotus flower,’ and ‘a person like a red lotus flower’? “It is in reference to the three stages of enlightenment, friend, that the Blessed One spoke thus: the stage of stream-entry, the stage of once-returning, and the stage of non-returning. For, friend, a person like a young jasmine flower has entered the stream and is incapable of falling away from the fruit of stream-entry. A person like a blue lotus flower has entered the stream and is incapable of falling away from the fruit of once-returning. A person like a red lotus flower has entered the stream and is incapable of falling away from the fruit of non-returning. It is in reference to these three stages of enlightenment, friend, that the Blessed One spoke thus: ‘a person like a young jasmine flower,’ ‘a person like a blue lotus flower,’ and ‘a person like a red lotus flower. This is what the venerable Ānanda said. Elated, that monk rejoiced in the words of the venerable Ānanda. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard. This is the meaning of what was said by the Blessed One, and thus it was understood by me. [End of Sutta 50] [The following suttas in this section follow the same structure, substituting the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arahantship for the respective flowers. [End of Chapter One]
Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
“Bhikkhus, there are these three roots of unwholesomeness.”
Greed as a root of unwholesomeness, hatred as a root of unwholesomeness, and delusion as a root of unwholesomeness—
these, monks, are the three roots of unwholesomeness.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
They destroy a person of evil mind,
like a tree with hollow bark that bears fruit.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
